writeup: TIC 318566745 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with 3.11% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 5.3 sigma significance, orbiting with a period of 37.476297 days. Pixel-level analysis confirms the transit signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 42.2, though the centroid offset of 1.0 arcsecond from the target warrants further investigation. A notable data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the initially measured period was half the true orbital period. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the automated detection pipeline assigns it a high probability score of 0.98 of being a genuine astrophysical target.
